title: Residents of Kissidougou mobilize over water and electricity shortages
scope: A local morning gathering in Kissidougou. The body read reports a plan to close the EDG and SEG offices, but does not establish the route or boundaries of the gathering.
organizer: Young and women leaders are named; the article identifies a spokesperson but no formal organization in the body read.
participants_original: The article describes young people and women mobilizing but gives no number or estimate.
threshold_50_evidence: The opened article confirms a collective gathering but provides no attendance count. The search-only word 'massively' in another result is unquantified; the 50-person threshold remains unestablished.

title.summary: The opened local report describes a morning mobilization over water and electricity service failures.

start_date.summary: The page update is dated 22 February 2021 and the article says the speakers went out 'today'; publication date and reported event day coincide in the text.

location.summary: The body locates the action in the urban commune of Kissidougou.

scope.summary: The account concerns one local gathering, but gives no route or physical perimeter. Other town reports remain search-only.

organizer.summary: The article names a spokesperson for young leaders; it does not identify a formal organizer in the body read.

demands.summary: Participants objected to water and electricity service failures and said they intended to close the EDG and SEG offices. These demands do not fit the available standardized demand categories, so the array is empty.

participants.summary: Young people and women are described as mobilized, but there is no numeric estimate.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The body-read S002 has no attendance count. Search-only S001 and S005 do not give a verified numeric estimate; S005's qualitative 'massively' wording cannot establish 50.

state_response.summary: The article reports tear-gas dispersal, then municipal and prefectural engagement at the utilities and contact with Conakry.

state_accommodation.summary: The mayor describes follow-up with EDG and SEG, and the prefect reports an EDG solution and SEG-funding talks. This records engagement, not a verified lasting resolution.

state_crowd_dispersal.summary: The article explicitly says gendarmes dispersed the gathering with tear gas.

state_ignore.summary: The same account describes mayoral and prefectural follow-up, so this specific report does not describe the authorities as ignoring the action.

state_target.summary: The opened event report names both EDG and SEG as intended office targets. EDG’s institutional page reproduces a 2019 decree establishing EDG as a public company; SEG’s status and either utility’s operational responsibility for the reported failures remain unverified.

notes: Participants sought reliable water and electricity service and said they planned to close the EDG and SEG offices. No standardized demand category directly captures utility-service reliability, so the demands array is empty. EDG’s institutional page reproduces a 2019 decree establishing EDG as a public company under the technical supervision of the Ministry of Energy and financial supervision of the Ministry of Economy and Finance. The event report also names SEG, whose legal status was not independently checked here. Local officials engaged after the action, but a lasting concession is unverified. S001, S003, S004 and S005 are search-only reports of the same event; origin and independence are unresolved. No crowd pooling across towns is applied.
open_questions: Find credible attendance evidence sufficient to assess the 50-person threshold.
Establish the physical end and any subsequent gatherings or recurrence.
Review the remaining Kissidougou reports for same-story origin and independent attendance/response evidence.
Verify SEG ownership and both utilities’ responsibility for the reported service failures; the EDG decree documents institutional status, not the February 2021 outage.

title: Faranah youth protest a prolonged electricity outage
scope: The opened report describes a group from Tonkolonko 2 blocking the Faranah–Kissidougou national road and another group entering town. Their coordination and whether they were one or multiple separate gatherings are not established.
organizer: Youth from Tonkolonko 2 are named; no formal organization is identified.
participants_original: The source gives no protester count. It reports nearly ten road barriers and says more than 100 vehicles were delayed; vehicle numbers are not a protester count.
threshold_50_evidence: The opened report gives no number or qualitative crowd-size estimate. Nearly ten barricades and more than 100 delayed vehicles do not establish 50 participants.

title.summary: The opened local report describes Faranah youth demanding restored electricity after a prolonged outage.

start_date.summary: The article gives the date as 24 February 2021 and says the first group took to the street at 07:00.

location.summary: The report identifies Tonkolonko 2, the Faranah–Kissidougou road and Faranah town.

scope.summary: One report describes two groups in town; shared organizing or a single crowd is not established.

organizer.summary: The report describes youth from Tonkolonko 2 and names no formal organization.

demands.summary: Participants sought restored electricity after nearly a week without service. The text is preserved in notes because there is no matching standardized demand category.

participants.summary: No participant count is supplied; the more-than-100 number refers to delayed vehicles.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No attendance estimate appears; vehicles and barricades are not a substitute for protester counts.

state_response.summary: The article reports security dispersal with tear gas and later negotiations/mediation by the mayor and autonomous battalion commander.

state_accommodation.summary: The mayor and battalion commander negotiated after the protest; this is coded as official engagement, not as a concession or service restoration.

state_crowd_dispersal.summary: The article says security forces dispersed a group with tear gas.

state_ignore.summary: The report describes official negotiations and mediation, so it does not describe officials as ignoring this action.

state_target.summary: The event report documents a demand for restored electricity but does not name the responsible utility. EDG's page reproduces a 2019 decree establishing EDG as a public company; the link between EDG's regional service and this Faranah outage still needs confirmation.

notes: Participants sought restoration of electricity after nearly a week without service. No standardized demand category directly captures this utility-service demand, so the demands array is empty. Do not treat more than 100 delayed vehicles as protesters, combine the two described groups, or merge this action with Kissidougou. S009 and S010 are search-only reports that appear to concern the same Faranah episode; their independence or story origin is unknown. The EDG page supplies institutional context only; it does not establish EDG responsibility for this exact outage.
open_questions: Find any attendance estimate and determine whether at least 50 people assembled.
Verify that EDG operated the relevant electricity service in Faranah at the time of the event.
Resolve whether the two groups in the article were coordinated or separate gatherings.
Find the physical end, whether electricity returned, and any further gathering.
Review S009 and S010 for written origin, independence and event details; preserve search-only status until a gated body review.

title: Fria bakers stop work over the official bread price
scope: The body-read account says all bakeries in Fria were closed from 12 through 15 February. It does not count bakeries or workers and describes no street gathering.
organizer: Bakers in Fria; no named union is identified in the body-read account.
participants_original: The article says all bakeries were closed but gives no number of bakeries, bakers or workers participating.
threshold_50_evidence: The reported townwide bakery closure is collective action, but the article gives neither a count of bakeries or participating workers nor a public gathering estimate. The 50-person threshold is not established.

title.summary: The body-read article reports a 72-hour bakery stoppage in Fria and bakers raising the loaf price after an official instruction.

start_date.summary: The report says bakeries were closed from 12 February.

end_date.summary: The report describes closures through 15 February; no later end is inferred for the price dispute.

location.summary: The account locates the closure and price dispute in Fria commune.

scope.summary: The article says all bakeries were closed from 12–15 February, but provides no count of bakeries or workers and reports no street assembly.

organizer.summary: The account attributes the action to bakers but does not identify a union or formal organization.

demands.summary: The article reports officials instructing bakers to keep the loaf at 3,000 GNF, followed by a 3,500 GNF price on 16 February. The price-policy category is provisional; no separately worded formal demand is quoted.

participants.summary: No number of bakers, workers or bakeries is given.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No count or attendance estimate is reported; saying all bakeries were closed does not quantify workers or establish a 50-person assembly.

state_response.summary: The article reports an official meeting and price instruction; it does not describe arrests, violence or dispersal.

state_accommodation.summary: Commerce and local officials met with bakers, which documents receipt/negotiation; it does not show an official concession.

state_ignore.summary: The reported official meeting and price instruction mean the account does not describe officials as ignoring the action.

state_target.summary: The article ties the dispute to an instruction by commerce/local officials to maintain a 3,000 GNF loaf price; whether bakers stated a formal policy demand is not reported.

notes: The demands array provisionally represents a dispute over the official bread price; the article says bakers raised the loaf price from the instructed 3,000 GNF to 3,500 GNF. It does not quote a separate formal demand or report a street assembly. S016 is a search-only January Fria bakery lead; continuity is unverified.
open_questions: Find any baker/workforce count and determine whether an assembly or other qualifying action of at least 50 participants occurred.
Verify whether the bakers stated a demand to change official price policy or whether the event is better represented as a work stoppage over regulated prices.
Review the January 30 Fria bakery report and later coverage before asserting continuity with this February stoppage.
